M5_vs_GT_same_L.interpretation: Every measured same-L M5 point improves Recall but adds measured time. It is a Recall/speed trade-off relative to GT, not a same-L joint improvement or a general losslessness theorem.

objective_observations.cross_L_scope: Exactly two discrete WebVid Recall@1 measured pairs dominate GT by Recall and median QPS. No such measured pair for WebVid Recall@100 or either Yandex K. No interpolation and no inference that both K metrics jointly improve at those lower L.

report_verdict: Final analysis_v2 report values and scope are correct. A broader summary must separate same-L Recall/speed trade-offs from the two actual WebVid K1 cross-L advantages and avoid saying M5 universally replaces GT.
limitations: No native run repeated by this reviewer; startup loaded-base and full 10K M5 linear merge guarantees are checked as final native receipts plus previously reviewed source, not newly replayed experiments.
Formal timing outputs are discarded by design; this audit checks saved full plain responses, source body parity and round receipts, not separate bit identity for every timed packet.
No full database/index hash reread in this audit; startup loaded-base check and existing frozen identity records are retained.
Confidence interval fields are checked for descriptive scope and CSV consistency; no independent bootstrap recomputation or population guarantee is claimed.
Historically exposed public test windows are not a new blind IID confirmation.
Cross-L dominance is descriptive on five measured L points; its QPS comparison is a ratio of point medians, not the same-L paired-ratio statistic.
Plots are not reviewed here and will be handled after their final completion.
